title: Hydrogen replaces helium as wafer backside coolant and carrier gas
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter change, resolving 'need a high-conductivity heat-transfer gas' vs 'helium is scarce': switch electrostatic-chuck backside cooling and CVD/ALD carrier flows from He to H2 (D2 where isotope passivation helps) at 5-20 Torr, where H2 conducts heat as well as or better than He (0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K). Leak rates stay below the flammability limit by design, supply comes from on-site electrolysis, and exhaust goes to the existing burn abatement.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30%, offline since March 2026). Backside cooling and carrier gas are the largest fab He uses, so this could remove ~60-80% of fab He demand.

title: Harvest helium and neon from the fab's own nitrogen plant
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: a mega-fab's on-site air-separation unit already processes ~100k Nm3/h of air for nitrogen. Add a non-condensable stripping column and a small cryo-adsorber that co-produce crude Ne (18 ppm in air) and He (5 ppm), then purify both on site, so rare-gas production merges into a plant the fab already runs.
why: Makes neon (litho lasers, a Ukraine-exposed supply) and part of the helium a domestic byproduct: a few thousand Nm3/yr of He and ~10k Nm3/yr of Ne per fab ASU, covering laser gas and leak checking.

title: Cryogenic helium bank filled from the fab's own exhaust
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: pipe He-bearing exhaust from leak-check stations, load locks and chuck fore-lines into a header, upgrade it with a polymer membrane, and adsorb it on activated carbon chilled by the fab's existing LN2. The fab builds a 3-6 month He buffer and releases it during supply shocks.
why: Turns helium from a just-in-time import into a buffered resource that is ~70-90% recycled, so wafer starts are insulated from events like the Qatar outage.

title: Pre-formed porous cleave layer makes CZ wafers reusable donors
idea: TRIZ #10 Prior action: before any device processing, anodize a double-porosity silicon layer into a prime CZ wafer and grow 3-5 um of device-grade epitaxial silicon on top (ELTRAN-style). After the array front-end, the wafer is bonded to a carrier or periphery wafer and cleaved at the porous layer, and the donor is re-polished and reused 10-20 times.
why: The DRAM active layer is a few um of a 775 um wafer, so this cuts CZ ingot, polysilicon energy and HPQ crucible use per wafer by ~5-10x.

title: Re-fuse spent crucible cullet into outer walls of new crucibles
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity, rebuilding crucibles from crucibles: crush spent devitrified CZ crucibles, acid-leach the silicon residue, and arc-fuse the cristobalite cullet into the structural outer layer of new crucibles. Only a 2-3 mm inner layer, the part that touches the melt, uses virgin Spruce Pine or synthetic quartz.
why: HPQ chokepoint (Spruce Pine >80%). The outer layer is ~70-80% of crucible mass, so virgin HPQ per crucible drops ~3-4x.

title: Continuous-recharge Czochralski stretches one crucible across many ingots
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: grow 300 mm DRAM-grade crystal by continuous CZ. Granular polysilicon feeds through a weir-partitioned double crucible while a magnetic field (MCZ) holds oxygen and melt height constant, giving 5-10 ingots per crucible instead of 1-2.
why: Crucibles per wafer fall 3-5x, which eases the HPQ chokepoint. Flatter axial oxygen and dopant profiles add ~15% usable ingot length.

title: Barrierless molybdenum buried wordline from a fluorine-free precursor
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out: deposit Mo by ALD/CVD from MoO2Cl2 (no WF6) directly in the buried-wordline trench. Without fluorine there is nothing to attack the gate oxide, so the 2-3 nm TiN barrier that W needs can be removed, and at 10-15 nm widths Mo's shorter electron mean free path gives lower resistance than TiN/W.
why: Takes China-dominated tungsten (~80%) and WF6 out of the cell array, for ~20-30% lower wordline RC or a ~2 nm narrower trench at the same RC.

title: Cold-trap recovery of unreacted ALD metal precursors
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: put fore-line cryotraps and a valve synchronized to the precursor pulses on ALD chambers. The ~90-95% of metal-organic precursor (TEMAZr, TEMAHf, TDMAT, Ru/Co organometallics) that normally burns in abatement is condensed into returnable canisters for the supplier to redistill.
why: Cuts Hf, Zr, Ru and Co precursor demand per wafer ~3-10x. The ZAZ/HZO capacitor stack is among the highest-cycle-count ALD steps in DRAM.

title: Area-selective deposition grows features only where needed
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: use inhibitor monolayers (aminosilanes or small-molecule inhibitors) that block ALD on dielectric but not on metal. Landing-pad caps, contact liners and bitline spacers then self-align by growth instead of by litho + etch, deleting a resist coat, a fluorocarbon etch and a mask for each layer replaced.
why: Less PFAS-bearing resist and fluorinated greenhouse gas, and 1-2 fewer EUV/ArFi exposures per node, which lowers both capital and chemical intensity.

title: Electrochemical hydrogen pump recycles EUV scanner hydrogen
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: route each EUV scanner's source and collector hydrogen exhaust (hundreds of slm) through a tin trap and a proton-exchange electrochemical hydrogen pump. The pump compresses and purifies the H2 and returns it to the scanner feed, so the tool supplies most of its own hydrogen.
why: Cuts H2 purchase per scanner ~80% along with the energy to make it, lowers EUV operating cost, and frees hydrogen for helium substitution.

title: Retired server DIMMs reharvested into pooled CXL memory
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round, memory flowing back up the supply chain: hyperscalers return DDR4/DDR5 from decommissioned servers to a qualification line. The line desolders the DRAM, retests it at speed and temperature, bins it by retention class, and rebuilds it onto CXL Type-3 expander cards for capacity tiers.
why: Adds usable DRAM supply with zero wafers, at ~30-50% of the cost per bit of new parts. A large share of retired server DRAM is still functional.

title: Cryogenic CO2-argon aerosol cleaning replaces wet rinse steps
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transitions: replace selected post-CMP and pre-deposition wet-clean, rinse and dry steps with a cryogenic aerosol of solid CO2/Ar micro-crystals. The crystals knock particles off by momentum transfer and then sublime, leaving no liquid or residue.
why: Cuts UPW and IPA per wafer pass (~10-20% of fab UPW in the targeted steps) and removes capillary forces that collapse 60-75:1 capacitor pillars.

title: Fab load-shifting using UPW and liquid nitrogen as energy storage
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: run the power-hungry subsystems that can be buffered (ASU liquefaction, UPW reverse osmosis, chiller ice making) in pulses during cheap renewable or nuclear hours. Their output is stored in LN2 dewars, UPW tanks and ice banks, so grid draw is periodic while the process tools run continuously.
why: Energy intensity: ~15-25% of fab load becomes flexible, for ~10% lower energy cost and access to U.S. sites with weaker grids.

title: Back-grind swarf from HBM thinning recycled into silicon feedstock
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: grinding HBM core dies from 775 um to ~40 um turns ~95% of each wafer (~120 g) into fine swarf. Collect it in a dedicated closed DI loop, strip the oxide shell with HF, and plasma-melt it into silicon feedstock for CZ recharge or solar.
why: Recovers most of the silicon, and its embedded polysilicon energy, from HBM wafers that is landfilled today. HBM uses ~3x the wafer area per bit, so the waste is growing fast.

title: Laser-sliced HBM wafer bodies reused as bonding carrier wafers
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation through the thickness: instead of grinding away 700 um, focus a sub-bandgap infrared laser ~80 um below the device side to write a modified plane (as KABRA does for SiC), then split the wafer. The ~650 um body is re-polished and reused as the temporary carrier wafer that HBM thinning and TSV reveal already require.
why: Halves virgin silicon demand on HBM lines (device wafer plus carrier) and removes most of the grinding time, wheel wear and slurry water.

title: Mold compound becomes the substrate, deleting ABF and T-glass
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: embed LPDDR/DRAM dies face-down in a reconstituted epoxy-mold wafer and build the redistribution layers directly on it (fan-out wafer-level packaging). Each die nests inside its own package body, so neither organic build-up laminate (Ajinomoto ABF) nor low-CTE T-glass cloth (Nittobo) is needed.
why: Removes two near-single-supplier packaging chokepoints from memory modules and mobile DRAM, for ~20-30% lower package cost and lead time.

title: Microsecond flash anneal crystallizes strontium titanate on bare TiN
idea: TRIZ #21 Skipping (rushing through the harmful window): deposit amorphous SrTiO3 by ALD on TiN and crystallize it with a ~1 ms flash-lamp pulse. The film reaches perovskite crystallization temperature before the TiN has time to oxidize into a low-k TiOx interlayer, which removes the Ru electrode that SrTiO3 capacitors historically needed.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): k ~100-150 vs ~40 for ZAZ allows ~2x Cs or a pillar aspect ratio cut from ~70:1 to ~35:1, with no Hf or Ru (Sr, Ti and O are abundant).

title: Per-recipe scarcity ledger that feeds back into process engineering
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: meter each tool's use per wafer of He, ALD precursors, fluorinated gases, UPW and kWh. Price each at a shadow scarcity cost (e.g., helium at its outage price) inside the fab's cost-per-bit model, so recipe changes are scored and rewarded on scarce-resource reduction.
why: Sustained sub-metering feedback has delivered 20-40% resource cuts in energy programs. This applies the same loop to every chokepoint input at once.

title: Bond a mature-node periphery wafer under the array
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension: move sense amps, decoders and I/O (~49% of the die) to a separately processed 28-40 nm CMOS wafer that is hybrid-bonded beneath the cell array. The array wafer then needs no Hf-based HKMG and fewer metal layers.
why: Raises bits per array wafer ~1.6-1.9x, removes Hf HKMG from the array fab, and lets periphery run in existing U.S. mature-node fabs (capital and U.S. manufacturability).

title: Thermal-expansion valves cut idle purge-gas flows automatically
idea: TRIZ #37 Thermal expansion: fit tool gas lines with passive bimetal or shape-memory valves keyed to chamber-wall or heater temperature. When a chamber idles and cools, the valve throttles He, N2 and H2 purge to a trickle, and it reopens as the heaters ramp, with no software change or recipe requalification.
why: Idle purge is often 20-40% of process-gas use, so this cuts He and N2 consumption and the ASU energy behind it by a similar share.

title: Electrolytically regenerated persulfate replaces sulfuric-peroxide wet strip
idea: TRIZ #38 Strong oxidants: replace single-pass SPM (H2SO4 + H2O2) resist strip and organic clean with an electrolyzed-sulfuric loop. Boron-doped-diamond anodes continuously regenerate peroxodisulfate from the same acid, so it is recirculated instead of drained.
why: Cuts sulfuric acid and peroxide purchase, neutralization chemicals and rinse water ~80-90%, which simplifies chemical logistics for new U.S. sites.

title: Dead-bank harvesting turns partial DRAM dies into lower-capacity SKUs
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial or excessive action: instead of scrapping dies whose repair redundancy runs out in a few banks, fuse those banks off. Sell the dies as 3/4- or 7/8-capacity parts with a mode register the controller maps around, as CPU makers do with harvested cores.
why: Raises usable bits per wafer ~2-6% at zero capital. The gain is largest for HBM, where one bad die scraps an entire stack.

title: Drop-tower silicon spheres skip crucibles, ingots and wire saws
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality: melt granular polysilicon droplets in a drop tube so they solidify without a crucible into 1-2 mm single-crystal spheres (the Ball Semiconductor route). Pattern small memory chiplets on each sphere with conformal maskless lithography, and pack the spheres into 3D memory clusters.
why: Removes HPQ crucibles, ingot pulling and kerf loss (~40% of silicon) for small-die memory, for up to ~50% lower cost per wafer-equivalent if curved-surface lithography is solved.

title: Self-oxidized TiN skin seeds rutile titania capacitor dielectric
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: oxidize the top 1-2 nm of the TiN bottom electrode with a controlled O3/plasma pulse into rutile TiO2 that serves as its own template, then grow Al-doped TiO2 by ALD so it crystallizes as rutile (k ~80). The whole stack is Ti, Al, N and O.
why: Breaks the 'smaller cell but more charge' contradiction without Ru templates or Hf/Zr. k ~2x ZAZ gives ~2x Cs, or the pillar aspect ratio can fall from ~70:1 to ~40:1.

title: Fe/Cr/Fe exchange stack builds cobalt- and ruthenium-free MRAM
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying the original 1988 GMR system: use Fe/Cr/Fe RKKY coupling as the synthetic antiferromagnet in place of Co/Ru/Co, and an Fe(001)/MgO(001)/Fe coherent-tunneling junction with interface perpendicular anisotropy. Mn-N pinning and TiN seed layers replace Ta, W and Pt.
why: STT-MRAM gives ~10-30 ns, refresh-free memory with ~1e12+ endurance, built only from Fe, Cr, Mn, Mg, Ti, N and O. A U.S. line would carry no Co, Ru, Ta, W or Pt exposure.

title: Zirconium disulfide channel with its own oxide as gate dielectric
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: 2D ZrS2 (bandgap ~1.7 eV) oxidizes easily, which is normally a defect. Here a controlled O2 plasma deliberately converts the top layers into amorphous ZrO2 (k ~20) that serves as a perfect-interface gate dielectric, giving a 2-3 layer ZrS2 write transistor for a 2T0C gain cell.
why: Replaces IGZO (In, Ga) in capacitor-less gain cells with Zr, S and O only. An atomically thin channel with native high-k targets sub-aA leakage at <=400 C, compatible with stacking 3D tiers.

title: Hydrogen-terminated diamond access transistor doped by vanadium oxide
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter change (raise the bandgap from 1.1 to 5.5 eV): grow nanocrystalline diamond at <=500 C, hydrogen-terminate it, and cap it with V2O5, whose deep electron affinity pulls a 2D hole gas into the surface (surface-transfer doping), sealed under Al2O3. The channel needs no dopants and its off-state leakage is negligible.
why: Attacks the <=13 fA leakage tail that forces refresh (fact 3). Retention could stretch from 64 ms to seconds or more, cutting refresh energy (16-33% of idle power) by >90%, using only C, H, V, Al and O.

title: Magnesium-zinc-silicon oxide replaces IGZO in gain cells
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite materials, giving each IGZO job to an abundant cation: Zn 4s orbitals provide the conduction path (indium's role), Si binds oxygen strongly to suppress vacancies (gallium's role), and Mg widens the gap to ~4 eV for lower leakage. The amorphous Mg-Zn-Si-O channel is deposited by ALD supercycles.
why: Removes In (byproduct-limited) and Ga (China ~98%) from oxide-semiconductor DRAM roadmaps at equal or lower off-current. Its ~5-15 cm2/Vs mobility is enough for write transistors.

title: Fully silicided titanium wordline grown inward from polysilicon fill
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: instead of depositing metal into the buried-wordline trench, fill the trench with doped polysilicon and convert it in place, top-down, into C54 TiSi2 (Ti deposition, Si pre-amorphization, two-step RTA). The conductor is grown from what is already there.
why: Removes W, WF6 and the TiN liner from the array. TiSi2 (~15 uOhm-cm bulk) approaches W at these widths, survives ~850 C and uses only Ti and Si.

title: Electromagnetic cold-crucible Czochralski eliminates the quartz crucible
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution (a field replaces the vessel): hold the melt in a segmented water-cooled copper crucible where induction currents heat and partly levitate it inside a frozen silicon skull, so silicon touches only silicon. Gettering oxygen is added deliberately through O2/H2O partial pressure, and nitrogen doping restores wafer strength.
why: Removes the HPQ crucible chokepoint (Spruce Pine >80%) and crucible-borne metal contamination, using only Si, Cu, O and N.

title: Acid-leached rice-husk silica as high-purity crucible feedstock
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: the crucible is single-use anyway, so source its silica from a cheap renewable stream. Leach rice husks with HCl/oxalic acid to strip K, Ca and Fe, burn them under controlled oxidation to amorphous SiO2, chlorine-purify the ash at ~1000 C, and arc-fuse it into crucible inner layers.
why: Diversifies HPQ away from Spruce Pine using U.S. Gulf-coast husk (~0.3 Mt/yr of silica available), targeting 5N purity at below mined-HPQ cost. Uses only Si, O, Cl, C and H.

title: Anodized mesoporous silicon electrodes multiply capacitor area
idea: TRIZ #31 Porous materials: anodize heavily doped silicon electrode arms in HF to form 3-5 nm mesopores, line the pores with ALD Al2O3/TiO2 nanolaminate, and fill them with TiN, so each electrode becomes a sponge with ~3-10x the surface area.
why: Reaches the needed Cs at an aspect ratio of ~20:1 instead of ~70:1, or makes lateral 3D-DRAM capacitors ~3x shorter, with no exotic high-k (Si, Al, Ti, N, O, F only).

title: Nested conductive-core insulating-shell nanograins give colossal effective k
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: build the dielectric from ~3 nm semiconducting reduced-TiO2 grains, each wrapped by ALD in a 0.5 nm Al2O3 shell. The field drops only across the thin shells (an engineered version of CaCu3Ti4O12's internal barrier layers), so effective k could reach several hundred.
why: Targets fact 1's k ~70 requirement with Ti, Al and O only. The risk is that Maxwell-Wagner relaxation is too slow for ns access and that leakage percolates through the cores.

title: Hafnium-free antiferroelectric zirconia boosts charge near switching field
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transitions: tune pure tetragonal ZrO2 so its field-induced transition to the polar orthorhombic phase sits just above the array voltage. The plate is biased at the edge of that transition, where steep dP/dE gives ~1.5-2x charge per area over linear ZAZ.
why: Raises Cs at the same pillar aspect ratio (fact 1) using only Zr, Al, Ti, N and O. Operating short of full switching avoids hysteresis and keeps endurance at DRAM levels.

title: Undercritical ferroelectric zinc-magnesium oxide adds negative-capacitance boost
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial action: place a thin wurtzite Zn1-xMgxO ferroelectric (a 2021 discovery made only of abundant elements) in series with Al2O3 and deliberately keep it just short of switching. It then operates in its negative-capacitance region and raises total stack capacitance above that of the Al2O3 alone.
why: Could boost Cs ~1.5-3x at the same geometry with only Zn, Mg, Al and O. The risks are negative-capacitance stability and leakage at ns timescales.

title: Manganese oxide abrasive replaces rare-earth ceria in CMP
idea: TRIZ #38 Strong oxidants: use Mn2O3/MnO2 nanoparticles whose Mn3+/Mn4+ redox bonds to and breaks Si-O bonds, supplying the 'chemical tooth' that ceria provides via Ce3+/Ce4+. They replace ceria in STI and ILD planarization.
why: Removes ceria (a China-dominated rare earth) from DRAM's heavy STI/ILD CMP load. Mn is ~950 ppm in the crust and can be refined in the U.S.

title: Plasma-deposited organosilicon resist converts to glass under exposure
idea: TRIZ #32 Color changes (exposure switches the film's chemistry): plasma-deposit a solvent-free methylsilane film whose exposed areas photo-oxidize into SiO2-like glass, then dry-develop the unexposed film in a Cl2 plasma.
why: Removes PFAS photoacid generators, spin solvents and developer water, and avoids tin-oxo EUV resists. Uses only Si, C, H, O and Cl.

title: Copper-nanodot catalyzed chemical etching drills capacitor molds
idea: TRIZ #24 Intermediary: self-assembled Cu nanodots sink into silicon in HF/H2O2, each locally catalyzing dissolution beneath itself, so they drill holes of 100:1 or deeper at room temperature without plasma. The silicon mold is then oxidized or lined to form the capacitor template.
why: Replaces the most capital-heavy, fluorocarbon-hungry step (high-aspect-ratio mold etch) with a wet bath: ~10x lower tool capital and no C4F8/CF4. Uses only Cu, Si, H, O and F.

title: Abatement fluoride captured as synthetic fluorspar for HF regeneration
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: run fluorine-bearing scrubber effluent through lime crystallizers that precipitate high-purity CaF2 pellets instead of sludge. The pellets go back to an acid plant that regenerates electronic-grade HF with H2SO4, closing the fab's fluorine loop.
why: Fluorspar is China-dominated (~60%). Recovering ~50-70% of fab fluorine cuts that dependence and sludge disposal, using only Ca, F, S, H and O.

title: Supercritical CO2 with ozone replaces water rinse-and-dry cycles
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics and hydraulics: clean and dry wafers in pressurized supercritical CO2 carrying dissolved ozone and a little alcohol co-solvent, then recompress and reuse the CO2.
why: Cuts UPW and IPA use. Zero surface tension also ends pillar collapse, so taller capacitors become possible (fact 1); only C, O and H are involved.

title: Single aluminum film anodized into lines and dielectric together
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: deposit one blanket Al film and convert the spaces between future lines into anodic Al2O3 by through-mask electrochemical anodization. One material then serves as wire, via, dielectric and pad, with no metal etch and no damascene CMP.
why: Removes Ta/TaN barriers, Co liners, W vias and Cu plating from DRAM's relaxed-pitch upper metal layers, along with several etch/CMP tools. Uses only Al, O, Ti and N.

title: Graphene liner lets copper fill the buried wordline
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out: grow a 1-2 layer graphene diffusion barrier in the wordline trench by low-temperature plasma CVD, then fill with Cu. A ~0.4 nm barrier replaces ~3 nm of TiN, and Cu, the lowest-resistivity abundant metal, replaces W.
why: ~3x lower wordline resistance than TiN/W at ~10 nm width allows faster or lower-voltage wordlines (fact 10), with no W. Uses only C and Cu, plus Si and O.

title: Conformal graphite-foil chuck membrane cools wafers without backside gas
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics (a rigid chuck becomes compliant): face the chuck with a thin compliant pyrolytic-graphite or CNT-forest membrane that electrostatic force flattens against the wafer backside. Heat then flows through solid contact instead of through He-filled grooves.
why: Removes backside helium, the largest fab He use, entirely without the safety work that H2 needs. Uses only C on an AlN/Al2O3 chuck body.

title: Spinel and AlON plasma-facing coatings replace rare-earth yttria
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: coat etch-chamber walls, liners and focus parts with a graded stack: dense MgAl2O4 spinel or AlON at the plasma face, grading to Al2O3 at the substrate. Each layer is placed where its erosion resistance or adhesion is needed, replacing Y2O3 and YF coatings.
why: Removes yttrium (a China-dominated rare earth) from high-wear chamber parts and grades CTE to cut flaking particles. Uses only Mg, Al, O and N.

title: Silica-lined polyethylene replaces fluoropolymer ultrapure-water piping
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells and thin films: build UPW and chemical distribution from high-density polyethylene pipe whose inner wall carries a plasma-deposited SiOx/a-C:H barrier film. The film blocks leaching and particle shedding, the reasons PFA/PVDF (both PFAS) were chosen.
why: Removes PFAS fluoropolymers from the fab's largest-volume wetted plastics ahead of PFAS restrictions. Uses only C, H, Si and O.

title: Fast-track qualification protocol for abundant-element material swaps
idea: TRIZ #10 Preliminary action: a consortium pre-builds shared JEDEC test vehicles, accelerated-stress datasets and failure-physics models for each abundant-element substitute (TiSi2 for W, Mg-Zn-Si-O for IGZO, spinel for yttria). A fab can then qualify a swap with a ~6-month delta test instead of a 2-3 year full requalification.
why: Qualification time, not chemistry, is the real barrier to dropping Hf, W, Co, Ru, Ta, In and Ga. Cutting it ~4x de-risks supply shocks and favors U.S. Earth-abundant supply chains.
